chunks.content: # CLO Master Express Lesson 16: Summer Swimwear Special – 3D Swimwear Modeling and Scene Construction Tutorial This document details advanced techniques for 3D swimwear modeling in CLO, including panel sewing, chest pad adjustments, fabric elasticity, decorative elements, pose and simulation controls, and rendering special effects. It covers practical instructions, tool uses, and key settings for creating realistic swimwear and promotional scenes with CLO software. --- ## Panel Sewing and Chest Pad Construction This section explains how to sew swimwear panels, create and adjust chest pads, and apply negative pressure for a snug fit using CLO's simulation tools. - **Sewing Panels**: Select panels and use the sewing machine tool to stitch edges, aligning seams via alignment points on side panels, bottom panel, back panel, and shoulder lines. - **Chest Pad Setup**: - Harden the chest pad panel and position it on the chest area. - Apply negative pressure to ensure the pad attaches tightly to the model. - Reduce particle diameter and collision thickness for better shape control. - Draw inner lines on the chest pad and engrave an outer layer to create a double-layer thickness. - Use positioning balls to fix the pad and prevent movement during simulation. - Adjust fabric thickness to enhance chest fullness. - **Simulation**: - Open simulation to confirm tight attachment due to negative pressure. - Make incremental shape adjustments and fix the pad with positioning balls. - **Panel Joint Adjustments**: - Remove joints from certain panels and align others to shape the chest. - Freeze the chest after completion to prevent further changes. --- ## Negative Pressure and Fabric Elasticity in 3D Swimwear This section covers the use of negative pressure and fabric elasticity settings to prevent stretching and maintain garment shape during simulation. - **Negative Pressure**: - Access negative pressure in the panel property calculator; set to negative values to pull fabric tightly onto the model. - **Elasticity Settings**: - Select edges prone to stretching (e.g., front chest panel lines). - Enable elasticity and set elasticity proportion to 100% to prevent deformation and fabric stretching. - Elasticity ensures panels return to normal shape after simulation forces. - **Simulation Tips**: - Adjust elasticity before simulation for optimal garment fit. - Use elasticity to avoid unwanted panel stretching in tight-fitting swimwear. --- ## Creating Bandages and Decorative Effects This section explains how to make bandage-style decorations using panels, internal patterns, holes, and double-layer borders to strengthen areas prone to damage. - **Hole Conversion and Internal Patterns**: - Use the Blur tool to select holes on the bandage panel. - Convert selected holes into internal patterns. - Select closed internal lines and convert them into holes using the adjustment panel tool. - **Double-Layer Borders**: - Create a column layer for the inner circle of the panel. - Cut excess inner lines to form stable double-layer borders, preventing fabric adhesion and breakage. - **Collage Function for Hole Stability**: - Add new inner lines around holes to reinforce edges.
